top_story: U.S. strikes on Iranian missile, drone, and radar sites on 26 June triggered a rapid cycle of retaliation on 27 June, as Iran claimed attacks on U.S.-linked targets and Bahrain absorbed drone strikes it attributed to Tehran. The later strike on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz prompted fresh U.S. attacks by 27 June night, pushing the confrontation beyond a contained exchange and sharpening risks to Gulf shipping, civilian security, and already brittle regional confidence. In Gaza, Israeli attacks on tents sheltering displaced Palestinians continued through 28 June, killing more civilians already trapped by siege and deprivation, while new restrictions at Al-Aqsa and the Ibrahimi Mosque widened the sense of collective pressure. The regional picture is one of simultaneous military escalation and deepening civilian harm, with the Hormuz crisis and Gaza violence reinforcing a broader erosion of deterrence and public stability.
